mele#1.etymon_note: Wiktionary mele#1 (its etymology is only a query: "derived from meli (honey)?"); no POLLEX set for the colour, so no ancestor. Not mele#0 "song" (PNP *umele; curated). The only P&E melemele in POLLEX is a star name (MELE.2, PNP *mele "a star"), another etymon. Word melemele.
mele#1.gloss_source: Wiktionary mele#1 "to be yellow", melemele "light yellow"; Andrews–Parker 1922 mele adj. 2 "yellow; generally written melemele"

miki#0.etymon_note: POLLEX MITI.3A (PPN *miti "suck, lick up") and MITI.3B (PEC *miti "undertow, eddy, ebb", Māori miti "undertow") are one set; word aumiki "rip current". Not miki#1 "quick".
miki#0.gloss_source: Wiktionary miki#0 "to suck in; to recede" and aumiki etymology "receding"; POLLEX (P&E) "suck in; undertow"

miko.etymon_note: Wiktionary miko (one entry, no etymology) lists mikomiko as derived; Andrews brackets mikomiko [Miko, to be salty]. No POLLEX row, so no ancestor. The other Andrews miko senses (knotted, ensnared) are not used and not shown. Word mikomiko.
miko.gloss_source: Wiktionary miko "seasoned with salt, salted; tasty"; Andrews–Parker 1922 miko "seasoned with salt; savory; saltish"

mili.etymon_note: POLLEX MILI, PPN *mili "rub with flat of hand; caress", holds P&E mili and milimili in one set; Andrews brackets milimili [Mili, to handle]. No Wiktionary entry: the provisional id from the review, confirmed. The gloss prints only "handle, caress" from the three P&E words. Word milimili.
mili.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) mili "Handle … caress", milimili "To examine with interest or curiosity and admiration"; Andrews–Parker 1922 bracket "Mili, to handle"

moa.etymon_note: POLLEX MOA.1 PPN *moa "fowl"; words huamoa, moamahi, hakamoa (Andrews: haka + moa "a fowl"). Not MOA.4A (banana bud, dart game) nor moʻa "cooked".

moana#0.etymon_note: POLLEX MOANA PPN *moana "sea beyond the reef, ocean"; words moanakai, moanawai, ʻaumoana. Not moana#1 "chiefs' meeting place".

moe.etymon_note: POLLEX MOHE PPN *mohe "sleep"; words aumoe, halemoe, hikimoe, kikomoe, moehewa, moeone, moeʻino, moeʻuhane (DECISIONS A15: keep, P&E check).

moku.etymon_note: POLLEX MOTU.A ("severed") and MOTU.B ("island") are one set, as B9 says; every word uses island/district/ship: mokupuni, mokuʻāina, mokuhonua, mokukaua, mokulele, mokuluʻu, mokumāhu, holomoku.

momi.etymon_note: No POLLEX row; makamomi (Andrews bracket: maka eye + momi pearl). Not Andrews momi "swallow" (= moni).

mona.etymon_note: Base of momona (Wiktionary: doublet; Andrews: primitive form). POLLEX files only momona, under PPN *moo-mona "fat, rich, tasty", with a note PCP *mona; Wiktionary says PPN *mona. Ancestor of the bare form left blank. Word monakō.
mona.gloss_source: Wiktionary mona "fat" and monakō etymology ("sugar fat")

moʻa.etymon_note: POLLEX MAQOHA PPN *maqoha "cooked", Hawaiian flagged Phonologically Irregular (Wiktionary says the same); word moʻamaka.

moʻo.etymon_note: POLLEX MOKO.1A PPN *moko "lizard"; words kuamoʻo (Andrews and Wiktionary: kua back + moʻo lizard) and moʻolele (Andrews: moo, reptile).

moʻo#line.etymon_note: New stone: moʻo "line, succession, lineage", a separate root from moʻo "lizard" (DECISIONS B8); POLLEX has no set for it. Words moʻoaliʻi, moʻokanaka, moʻokupuna, moʻokūʻauhau, moʻoʻōlelo.
moʻo#line.gloss_source: Andrews 1922 brackets "moo, a line" (moʻokūʻauhau, moʻoaliʻi, moʻokupuna, moʻoʻōlelo) and moo n. 3 "a line"; DECISIONS B8 "succession"

mua.etymon_note: POLLEX MUQA.A PPN *muqa "front, before"; words hānaumua, makamua.
mua.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) "before, ahead, front"; Wiktionary "first, in front"

muli.etymon_note: POLLEX MURI.1A PPN *muri "behind, after, be last" (MURI.1C "young" is the same set); word mulihope (Andrews: muli last + hope end).

māhu.etymon_note: POLLEX MA-QAFU.1 PNP *ma-qafu "steam, steamy"; word mokumāhu. A different stone from māhū (DECISIONS A17).
māhu.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) "to steam, exude vapour"; Wiktionary "steam, vapor"

mākaʻi.etymon_note: POLLEX MAATA-KI PPN *maata-ki "visit, inspect, observe" (Wiktionary's mā- + kaʻi analysis is not followed); word halemākaʻi.

māmā.etymon_note: POLLEX MAQA-MAQA.A PPN *maqa-maqa "light in weight"; word akemāmā (ake + light). Not Andrews mama "chew".

mū#2.etymon_note: The game sense has no POLLEX set (POLLEX MUMU "crowded together" covers only "gathered together", flagged Problematic). Wiktionary's group also holds a captor sense that is never shown (DECISIONS A17). Word papamū.
mū#2.gloss_source: Wiktionary mū#2 "kōnane; checkers" and papamū etymology

mū#4.etymon_note: POLLEX MUU.3A, PNP *muu "be silent", and Wiktionary mū#4 from the same. The cognates in the set include murmuring (Māori, Tahitian), so the "hum" of mūmū fits it. Not P&E mūmū "dull, blunt" (MUU.4, PCE *muu "blunt"), a separate set, and not mū#0 insect, mū#2 (kōnane; curated, A17) or mū#3 fish. The spelling mūmū for this sense is inferred (Andrews writes no kahakō): P&E to confirm. Word mūmū.
mū#4.gloss_source: Wiktionary mū#4 "silent"; POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) mū "Silent; to shut the lips and make no sound"; Andrews–Parker 1922 mumu "to be silent", "to hum"

nahe.etymon_note: Andrews has nahe as its own headword (adj. and v.) and calls nahenahe "same as nahe". Wiktionary and POLLEX derive only the doubled word, PPN *ŋase-ŋase "weak, feeble", so no ancestor is printed on the single stone; the cognates are the doubled forms in that set. The provisional id from the review, confirmed; P&E should confirm nahe as a free word. Word nahenahe.
nahe.gloss_source: Andrews–Parker 1922 nahe "soft; gentle, as the voice of music; to blow softly" (placeholder until P&E); POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) nahenahe "Soft, gentle, suave"; Wiktionary nahenahe "soft; sweet, melodious"

nahele.etymon_note: POLLEX GASERE PCE *ŋasere "forest"; word makanahele (Andrews: maka face + nahele the wild).

nalu#0.etymon_note: POLLEX GALU.1 PPN *ŋalu "wave of sea"; words heʻenalu, heiheinalu. POLLEX RANU.B (*ranu) is another etymon and is never shown (DECISIONS A16).

nau.etymon_note: POLLEX GAU, PPN *ŋau "chew to extract juice; bite". No Wiktionary entry: the provisional id from the review, confirmed. Separate from P&E naunau "a medicinal plant" (POLLEX NAU.1, PNP *nau), which is the only P&E naunau in hand, so the chewing sense of naunau rests on Andrews ([Nau, to bite]) and needs P&E. The other Andrews nau entries (gardenia, sadness, the possessive) are other words. Word naunau.
nau.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) nau "Chew"; Andrews–Parker 1922 nau "to chew; … to bite"

naʻau.etymon_note: POLLEX GAAKAU PPN *ŋaakau "intestines" (seat of thought); words naʻauao, naʻaupō, naʻaulua, naʻaupono, paʻanaʻau.
naʻau.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) "intestines; mind, heart, affections"; Wiktionary "guts; mind, heart"

naʻi#0.etymon_note: POLLEX GAKI.B PCE *ŋaki "avenge, conquer"; word hōkūnaʻi. GAKI.A (naʻi#1 "strive") is the same set.
naʻi#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) "conquer, take by force"; Wiktionary hōkūnaʻi etymology "conquering star"

nihi.etymon_note: POLLEX NIFI.1 PPN *nifi "thin, sharp" (Hawaiian edge); word kūnihi. Not NIFI.2 "move stealthily".
nihi.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) "edge, brink, rim; standing on edge"; Andrews 1922 bracket "nihi, to turn edgeways"

niho.etymon_note: POLLEX NIFO, PPN *nifo "tooth"; Wiktionary agrees and lists nihoniho as derived. Word nihoniho (toothed, serrated).
niho.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) niho "Tooth"; Wiktionary niho "tooth; ivory; tusk"

nini#1.etymon_note: Wiktionary-only sense with no etymology (Andrews nini v. 4 "to face or cover with stone" is near); not POLLEX NIGI/NINI.3 "pour; ointment" (nini#0). Word pānini, a P&E check.
nini#1.gloss_source: Wiktionary nini#1 "fence, line of stones" and pānini etymology

niu#0.etymon_note: POLLEX NIU.1 PPN *niu "coconut palm"; words hāniu, ʻaʻaniu. Not NIU.2 "spinning" (niu#1).

noho.etymon_note: POLLEX NOFO PPN *nofo "sit, dwell"; words nohoaliʻi, nohopaʻa.
noho.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) "sit, dwell"; Wiktionary "seat; to sit, reside"

noʻo.etymon_note: New stone for noʻonoʻo (was unresolved). Andrews has Noo as its own headword, "primitive form of noonoo … used only in noonoo", and brackets noonoo [Noo, to think]. A bound root with no Wiktionary entry and no POLLEX row, so no ancestor. The spelling noʻo is taken from noʻonoʻo (Wiktionary); Andrews writes no ʻokina. P&E to confirm. Word noʻonoʻo.
noʻo.gloss_source: Andrews–Parker 1922 noo "to seek … to reflect; to turn over and over …" and bracket "Noo, to think" (placeholder until P&E); Wiktionary noʻonoʻo "to think, reflect"

nui.etymon_note: POLLEX NUI.1 PNP *nui "big"; words alanui, ahonui, kuanui, manamananui.

nuku#0.etymon_note: POLLEX GUTU.A PPN *ŋutu "mouth, lip, beak, orifice"; word nukuwai. GUTU.B (nuku#1 "scold") is the same set.
nuku#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) "beak, snout, mouth (of harbour)"; Andrews 1922 bracket "nuku, mouth"

nānā#1.etymon_note: POLLEX NAA-NAA PCE *naa-naa "look at"; words kūnānā, nānāao, nānāuli.
nānā#1.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) "look at, observe"; Wiktionary "to look, observe"

nīnau.etymon_note: No POLLEX row; word kikonīnau (Andrews: kiko point + ninau question).

nū.etymon_note: POLLEX GUU.1, PPN *ŋuu "hum, groan, grunt"; Wiktionary nū (one entry, no etymology) "grunt; to cough, to roar". nūnū "pigeon, dove" is the bird named for its call (Andrews: nu "the cooing of doves", nunu "cooing like doves"), so the stone is this sound root; no source gives nūnū an etymology, so P&E should confirm. Word nūnū.
nū.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) nū "Cough, roar as the wind, grunt", hoʻonū "Moan, grunt, hum"; Andrews–Parker 1922 nu "the cooing of doves" (placeholder until P&E)

oka.etymon_note: POLLEX QOTA.2, PPN *qota "dregs, residue"; Wiktionary derives oka from it and okaoka from PPN *qota-qota; Andrews brackets okaoka [Intensive of oka, refuse]. The Andrews entries oka "oak" (English) and oka "decoy" are other words. Word okaoka.
oka.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) oka "Dregs"; Wiktionary oka "dregs, sediment; crumbs, small bits"

ola.etymon_note: POLLEX OLA.1 PPN *ola "be alive, well"; words kūola, laweola (Andrews brackets: ola life). Not Andrews olā "gurgle".

olo?olokaʻa.etymon_note: Unresolved: no source says which olo (POLLEX OLO.1 hill, OLO.2 resound, OLO.3 rub back and forth) or whether olo- is a formative. Word olokaʻa.
olo?olokaʻa.gloss_source: none: Andrews bracket [Olo and kaa, to roll] leaves olo unglossed

omo.etymon_note: POLLEX QOMO PEP *qomo "suck"; words omokoko, omoliu (Andrews brackets: omo, to suck).

one.etymon_note: POLLEX QONE PPN *qone "sand"; words kahaone, moeone, onehānau, oneʻā, puʻuone.

pae#1.etymon_note: POLLEX PAE.1B, PCE *pae "row, barrier, side"; Wiktionary pae#1 derives from it (< PPN *pae "heap of stones") with "platform" among its senses, and paepae from PPN *pae-pae "stone surround of a structure". Not pae#0 "come ashore" (PPN *paqe). The Andrews sense "to lift, to raise a little. See paepae" sits in his come-ashore pae entry, so the link to pae#1 rests on Wiktionary: P&E to confirm. Word paepae. The curated single stone paepae (paepae puka) is this same doubled word: see notes (B6).
pae#1.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) pae "Cluster, row, bank"; Wiktionary pae#1 "row; cluster, group; bank; … platform"

paepae.etymon_note: POLLEX PAE-PAE (PN) "stone surround of a structure", which has no Hawaiian row; Wiktionary assigns Hawaiian paepae to it. Word paepaepuka.
paepae.gloss_source: Wiktionary "platform; prop, support"; Andrews 1922 bracket "paepae, a platform"

pahu#0.etymon_note: POLLEX PASU.1B PCE *pasu "drum"; P&E has drum and box in one entry (Andrews: box from drum). POLLEX also files that entry under PPN *pusa "box", flagged Problematic. Words pahukani, pahupalapala.
pahu#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) "box, drum, cask, chest"; Wiktionary pahu#0

pahu?pahukapu.etymon_note: Unresolved: the shipped gloss (kapu marker) uses pahu "stake" while Andrews' Lit. says "sacred box"; sacred subject, so a P&E check and the kumu decide. Word pahukapu.
pahu?pahukapu.gloss_source: none settled: Andrews bracket "pahu, box" vs Andrews sense 2 "tabu stake" (pahu n. 3 "stake, post")

paio.gloss_source: Wiktionary "to fight, quarrel; contend"; Andrews 1922 bracket "paio, to contend"

paka#4.etymon_note: POLLEX PATA.1A, PPN *pata "raindrop" (Wiktionary calls paka#4 onomatopoeic; the POLLEX ancestor is printed). P&E pakapaka "wrinkled, scaly" is PATA.1B, a lettered sub-set of the same set, so no split (B8). Not paka#0 (strain; cartilage) or the English loans paka#1–#3. Words pakakahi (Andrews: [Paka, drop, as rain, and kahi, one]) and pakapaka (Andrews: [Paka, to drop] "to patter"); the rain sense of pakapaka is Andrews-only and needs P&E.
paka#4.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) paka "Raindrops, patter of rain, esp. big drops"; Wiktionary paka#4 "the sound of raindrops falling"; Andrews–Parker 1922 bracket "Paka, to drop"

palai#avert.etymon_note: New stone: Andrews' verb palai "turn the face away", neither the fern (PPN *palai "yam", palai#0) nor "fry" (from English, palai#1). No POLLEX row. Word palaimaka. Spelling and sense still need P&E.
palai#avert.gloss_source: Andrews 1922 palai v. "to be ashamed and turn the face away" and palaimaka bracket "palai, to turn away"

palapala.etymon_note: No POLLEX set for palapala. Wiktionary: reduplication of pala "to dab, to blot"; POLLEX pala sets (PALA.1A-C, 2, 3) are other homographs, so none is attached. Reduplicated stem as one stone (B7 b). Words kiʻipalapala, pahupalapala, papapalapala.
palapala.gloss_source: Wiktionary "printed patterns on kapa; print or document; writing of any kind"; Andrews 1922 "characters impressed on tapa or paper; a writing"

pale#0.etymon_note: Wiktionary files cover/lining with headdress (POc *pale2; POLLEX PALE.2 PPN *pale "head-dress", Marquesan "any head covering; cap"). Andrews files coverings under ward-off instead, but both POLLEX sets are PPN *pale, and Māori pare and Tongan pale are in both rows, so the printed line is right either way. Words palemaka, paleuhi (face veil, covering).
pale#0.gloss_source: Wiktionary pale#0 "headdress; cover; pad, lining"; Andrews 1922 bracket "pale, a garment / a covering" (palemaka, paleuhi)

pale#1.etymon_note: POLLEX PALE.1A PPN *pale "ward off; protection, defense"; P&E pale kai (breakwater) is POLLEX PALE-TAI PNP *pale-tai. Words palekai, palekaua, palekeiki (Andrews files "to deliver" under this verb).
pale#1.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) "ward off, thrust aside, parry, fend off"; Wiktionary pale#1 "to ward off; to protect"

pale?kaupale.etymon_note: Left unresolved, as the kau side was in batch-02: with the partition sense (Andrews) it is pale#1 "ward off"; with P&E sense (imu cover) it may be pale "lining" (pale#0). The P&E gloss chosen for the card decides.
pale?kaupale.gloss_source: none: Andrews bracket "pale, to ward off" (partition sense); POLLEX files P&E kaupale "to cover an oven ... to keep earth out" under TAU.12 *tau "cover" and leaves pale unassigned

pana.etymon_note: POLLEX PANA.1A PPN *pana "release something held under tension, recoil" (sub-sets 1B throb, 1C PMQ bow are the same set). Wiktionary traces the bow sense to PPN *fana; POLLEX files Hawaiian pana under *pana. Words panapua (shoot arrows), panapoʻo (flick or strike the head).
pana.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) "shoot (as marbles)"; Wiktionary "to shoot; to snap; to flip"; Andrews 1922 "to shoot, as an arrow"

pane.etymon_note: Wiktionary pane (one entry, no etymology); Andrews brackets panepane [Pane, to speak]. No POLLEX row for this sense, so no ancestor. Not pane#head "back of the head" (POLLEX PANE.A, PPN *pane; curated), whose ancestor is never printed here. Word panepane.
pane.gloss_source: Wiktionary pane "answer; to answer, reply"; Andrews–Parker 1922 pane "to utter; to speak; to answer; to reply"

pane#head.etymon_note: POLLEX PANE.A PPN *pane "blunt or knoblike projection"; P&E pane "hind part of the head". Not Wiktionary pane "answer" (no etymology), which no shipped word uses. Word panepoʻo.
pane#head.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) "hind part of the head; top or summit"; Andrews 1922 pane "the joining of the head with the bones of the neck"

pani.etymon_note: POLLEX PANI.2 PCE *pani "block up"; Wiktionary gives the same etymon. Words panipuka (door), panipū (wad of a gun), panipūpū (shell set as an eyestone).
pani.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) "close, shut"; Wiktionary "to close, to shut; plug, stopper; lid; gate, door"

papa#0.etymon_note: POLLEX PAPA.1A (PPN board), 1B (PPN flat hard surface) and 1C (PEP layer, stratum; list, genealogy; P&E "class, rank") are one set (B8/B9: link). Takes in papa#1: kūkulupapa uses "rank" (1C), keikipapa uses Andrews "papa, an ancestor" (1C genealogy). Words papamū, papakea, laupapa, papalalo, papawaena, kuapapa and the table words.
papa#0.gloss_source: Wiktionary papa ety. 1 "board, lumber; flat surface, layer; foundation; storey"; POLLEX (P&E) "board", "flat hard surface", "class, rank, grade, order"

pau.etymon_note: POLLEX PAU.1C PNP *pau "finished, over, ended", with 1D (PEP consumed, used up) and 1E (PCE all) in the same set; Sāmoan pau from 1C, Māori and Tahitian pau from 1D. Word pauaho (out of breath). Not paʻu "soot" (PAKU.C).
pau.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) "finished, ended, through"; "consumed, destroyed"; Wiktionary "finished, done; destroyed; all"

paʻa.etymon_note: POLLEX PAKA.1A PPN *paka "dried, scorched"; Wiktionary gives the same etymon. The hold-fast words (paʻahao, paʻawaha, paʻakāhili, paʻanaʻau) are the same entry in Andrews ("to be fast; to hold"). Words kinopaʻa, kūpaʻa, paʻakai, kōpaʻa, waiūpaʻa and 20 more.
paʻa.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) "firm, solid, tight ... hard, sound"; Wiktionary "solid; firm, fast, permanent"

paʻa?wahapaʻa.etymon_note: Left unresolved. Andrews ends the entry "o ka wahapaa, oia ka hoopaapaa", tying it to hoʻopaʻapaʻa "argue"; no source says whether that paʻa is paʻa "firm" (PAKA.1A). Not linked until P&E settles it.
paʻa?wahapaʻa.gloss_source: none: Andrews 1922 brackets "waha, mouth, and paa" with paa unglossed

paʻi.etymon_note: POLLEX PAKI.1 PPN *paki "slap, clap; hit, beat; touch"; Wiktionary gives the same etymon. Word paʻi kiʻi (print an image). Tahitian forms left out (POLLEX gives pāʻi/paʻipaʻi from a source that may not mark length).
paʻi.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) "slap, spank, beat, hit, clap"; Wiktionary "to hit; to slap; to clap; to print; to photograph"

paʻi?paʻiaʻa.etymon_note: Left unresolved. POLLEX files P&E paʻiaʻa "root system, rootlets" whole under PAKI-AKA PNP *paki-aka "root of a plant" (Māori pakiaka, Tahitian paiaa); the first element is not PAKI.1 "slap" and its sense is unknown, so it must not link to paʻi kiʻi.
paʻi?paʻiaʻa.gloss_source: none: Andrews 1922 bracket "pai and aa, small roots" leaves pai unglossed

paʻi?paʻiʻai.etymon_note: Left unresolved: Andrews writes pai "bundle" (no ʻokina marked) while the modern word is paʻi ʻai; no source shows a paʻi "bundle", and it must not link to paʻi "strike". Gloss is Andrews only (F1 placeholder).
paʻi?paʻiʻai.gloss_source: Andrews 1922 bracket "pai, a bundle, and ai, food" (paiai "bundle of pounded taro done up in ti leaves"); Hawaii News Now (via review)

peka.etymon_note: No Wiktionary entry and no POLLEX row for peka itself; the base is attested by Andrews headwords (adj. "censorious", v. "to speak evil of one absent") and named with the sense "tattle" in Wiktionary etymology of pekapeka, so the doubled word keeps the base sense. No ancestor known, none printed. New id "peka" (bare root, untaken), as the reviewer proposed. Word pekapeka; P&E should confirm peka as a free word.
peka.gloss_source: Wiktionary pekapeka etymology "reduplication of peka (tattle)"; Andrews–Parker 1922 peka v. "to speak of another in a fault-finding manner"

peku.etymon_note: POLLEX PETU PCE *petu "kick out"; Wiktionary gives the same etymon and has one homograph. The POLLEX row has no cognate in the six card languages, so none is printed. Word pekupeku (kick again and again).
peku.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Kick; ward off (as a spear)"; Wiktionary peku "to kick; kick"

pele.etymon_note: POLLEX files P&E pele under PERE.3 PTA *pere "dart", flagged Problematic; Wiktionary gives no etymology, so no ancestor is printed (the provisional *pere and Māori pere are dropped). Common noun only, never the goddess (DESIGN 4.3). Word luapele.
pele.gloss_source: Wiktionary "volcano"; POLLEX (P&E) "volcano, eruption, lava flow"; Andrews 1922 "a volcano"

pia#0.etymon_note: POLLEX PIA.1 PPN *pia "arrowroot (Tacca leontopetaloides); starch"; Wiktionary gives the same etymon. Not pia#1 "beer" (borrowed) or pia#2. Word haupia.
pia#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) "arrowroot, starch"; Wiktionary pia#0 "Polynesian arrowroot; starch"

piha.etymon_note: POLLEX files P&E piha under PISA.* PEP *pisa "box", flagged Uncertain Semantic Connection; Wiktionary gives no etymology, so no ancestor is printed (the provisional *pisa and Tahitian piha are dropped). Word pihalima (a handful).
piha.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) "full, complete, filled"; Wiktionary "full, filled; complete"; Andrews 1922 bracket "piha, full"

pili.etymon_note: POLLEX PILI.1A PPN *pili "adhere, stick to" and 1B PNP *pili "be close to, joined" are one set. Not PIRI-PIRI PCE *piri-piri, the pili grass, which the provisional entry had. Words kahapili (touching line, tangent), ʻikepili (data).
pili.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) "adhere to", "joined to"; Wiktionary "to cling, to stick; to join; to be close, associated; to relate to"

pio#2.etymon_note: Wiktionary onomatopoeic pio, one sense family (peep, chirp, whistle, pipe). Not pio#0 "extinguished" (POLLEX PIO PCE *pio, whose ancestor must not be printed here), pio#1 "captive" (nohopio, waiwai pio) or piʻo "arched" (other spelling). No ancestor, no cognates. Word piopio (chick, named for its peeping). The word is pending only for a sense Andrews lists under piopio (a sorcery prayer, §4.3); it belongs to the doubled word, not to this stone, and is never printed.
pio#2.gloss_source: Wiktionary pio#2 "peep, peeping; to peep, to chirp"; Andrews–Parker 1922 piopio v. "to peep, as a chicken"

pipi#seep.etymon_note: New stone for pīpīwai, resolving pipi?pipiwai: Andrews names pipi "to percolate" (pipi v. [Pi, to throw water]). Not Wiktionary pipi#0 pearl oyster (POLLEX PIPI.1 *pipi) or pipi#1 "beef". Spelled pīpī as in the word pīpīwai; id keeps the dossier key "pipi". Reduplicated stem, never linked to pī#sprinkle (B7 b, B10). No POLLEX set.
pipi#seep.gloss_source: Andrews 1922 pipiwai bracket "pipi, to percolate"; Andrews pipi v. "to sprinkle; to wet by sprinkling water"

piʻi#0.etymon_note: POLLEX PIKI.1B PEP *piki "climb, ascend"; Wiktionary gives the same etymon. Not piʻi#1 (short form of piʻipiʻi "curly" < PNP *piki-piki, of pipiʻi "expensive", and a gusset). P&E via POLLEX has only "climb, ascend"; Wiktionary vulgar sense is never printed (A4, default keep). Marquesan left out: its POLLEX gloss carries a sexual sense; Tahitian left out (modern spelling unsure). kai piʻi is POLLEX TAI-PII PCE *tai-pii "high tide"; P&E ʻokina fits piʻi < *piki ("rising"), not a *pii, so it stays on this stone. Words alapiʻi, kai piʻi, waipiʻi.
piʻi#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Climb, ascend"; Wiktionary piʻi#0 "to rise, to climb, to ascend"

piʻo.etymon_note: POLLEX PIKO.A PPN *piko "bent, curved, crooked"; Wiktionary gives the same etymon. Not pio "extinguished" (PIO, PCE *pio) nor Andrews pio "captive". Word halepiʻo.
piʻo.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) "bent"; Wiktionary "bend, curve, arc; to arch (of a rainbow)"; Andrews 1922 bracket "pio, an arch"

poe#0.etymon_note: POLLEX POE PEP *poe "pearl" (P&E poe "round, spherical"). Not the loans poe#1 "boy" and poe#2 "buoy", nor Andrews poe "company" (P&E poʻe, another spelling). Repeat poepoe is POE·POE on this stone; the first-pass one-stone "poepoe" (hulipoepoe, paʻapoepoe) stays its own stone and never links to poe#0 (§4.4).
poe#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Round (spherical)"; Wiktionary poe#0 "round, rounded"; Andrews–Parker 1922 poe adj. "round; circular"

poepoe.etymon_note: Reduplication of poe "round" (Wiktionary), whose POLLEX set is POE PEP *poe "pearl" (P&E poe "round, spherical"); one stone, never linked to a poe stone (B7 b). Words hulipoepoe, paʻapoepoe.
poepoe.gloss_source: Wiktionary "round, rounded; sphere, globe"; Andrews 1922 "round; globular"; POLLEX (P&E) poe "round (spherical)"

poi?hiʻipoi.etymon_note: Left unresolved. Andrews poi "to cover, protect" is the word P&E spells poʻi, a different spelling and stone; the food poi (POLLEX POQOI PPN *poqoi) is not attached because no source reads hiʻipoi that way. The provisional "porridge" gloss and *poqoi are dropped.
poi?hiʻipoi.gloss_source: none: Andrews 1922 bracket "hii and poi, to protect" (poi v. "to cover; to shut, as with a lid"); the popular reading is poi the food

pona.etymon_note: POLLEX PONA PPN *pona "knot, joint, swelling"; Wiktionary gives the same etymon. Not POGA.2/3 PNP *poŋa (socket; spotted). Word iwipona.
pona.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) "joint of sugarcane or bamboo stem"; Wiktionary "node of bamboo or sugarcane; joint of bones, fingers"; Andrews 1922 "the joints, as of the spine and fingers"

pono.etymon_note: POLLEX PONO.2 PCE *pono "true, correct"; Wiktionary says PPN *pono, probably an Eastern Polynesian innovation. Words kūpono, lelepono, naʻaupono.
pono.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) "correct procedure, correctness"; Wiktionary "goodness; correct procedure; good, moral, proper"

pouli.etymon_note: POLLEX POO-QULI PPN *poo-quli "dark night, darkness". Spelled pōuli: POLLEX gives P&E makapōuli (MATA-POOURI PCE *mata-poouri) and the long *poo, though its root row and Wiktionary write pouli; id "pouli" kept (B10). Word makapōuli.
pouli.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) "dark; darkness, dark night"; Wiktionary "darkness; eclipse"; Andrews 1922 bracket "pouli, darkness"

poʻo.etymon_note: Wiktionary derives poʻo "head" from PPN *qulu-poko (Tahitian poʻo, Māori upoko), but POLLEX lists no Hawaiian poʻo "head"; its poʻo rows are POKO.2 "cavity" and POKO.3 "slap water", other homographs, so no ancestor is printed. Twelve words, all "head".
poʻo.gloss_source: Wiktionary "head; summit; director"; Andrews 1922 "the head; the summit; a head, leader"

pua.etymon_note: POLLEX PUA.1B PEP *pua "to flower; flower, blossom" (1A PPN *pua, a tree with showy flowers, same set). Andrews derives "arrow" from the flowering sugar-cane tassel used as a dart, and Wiktionary keeps both on one entry, so one stone (B9). Words puakala, puapoʻo (flower); panapua, ʻaʻapua (arrow).
pua.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) "flower, blossom"; Wiktionary "flower; progeny; arrow, dart"; Andrews 1922 "a blossom; ... hence, an arrow"

puaʻa.etymon_note: POLLEX PUAKA PPN *puaka "pig"; Wiktionary gives the same etymon. Māori poaka left out (POLLEX flags it Problematic). Not pūʻāʻā "scattered". Words ahupuaʻa, kahu puaʻa.

puka.etymon_note: POLLEX PUTA.1A PPN *puta "aperture, hole" and 1B PCE "pass through, emerge" are one set; Wiktionary gives the same etymon. Words pukaihu, pukahale, puka makani, panipuka, kiaʻipuka, paepae puka.
puka.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) "hole; door, entrance, opening"; Wiktionary "hole, gate, doorway"

pule#0.etymon_note: POLLEX PULE.2 PPN *pule "have authority"; Wiktionary gives the same etymon. Not pule#1 "speckled" (cowrie, PULE.1). Words haipule, hale pule.
pule#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) "prayer, pray, grace, blessing"; Wiktionary pule#0 "prayer; to pray"

pule#1.etymon_note: POLLEX files P&E pulepule under PULE-PULE PPN *pule-pule "spotted" (doubled cognates across Polynesia, given here); POLLEX has no row for a single pule "speckled". Wiktionary derives pule#1 from PPN *pule "cowrie" (POLLEX PULE.1, set at MP level, Hawaiian only pūlehō, problematic). So the ancestor printed is *pule, the root of *pule-pule. Not pule#0 "prayer" (PULE.2 PPN *pule "have authority"): same ancestor spelling, different set, never linked. Word pulepule.
pule#1.gloss_source: Wiktionary pule#1 "speckled"; POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) pulepule "Spotted"; Andrews–Parker 1922 pulepule "spotted; speckled"

puna#0.etymon_note: POLLEX PUNA PPN *puna "bubble or well up; a spring". Not puna "coral, lime" (PUGA PPN *puŋa) or "internode" (PNP *puŋa), which Wiktionary puna#0 also lists. Words wai puna, hūpuna. Not pūnā of pūnāwai (B10).

puni#0.etymon_note: POLLEX PUNI.1A PPN *puni "prevent access by surrounding completely"; Wiktionary gives the same etymon. Words mokupuni, kaʻapuni, anapuni, kūpuni, pōʻai puni.
puni#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) "surrounded; completed"; Wiktionary puni#0 "surrounded, enclosed"; Andrews 1922 "around; on every side"

puni#1.etymon_note: Wiktionary keeps "fond of" apart from puni#0 and gives no etymology; POLLEX has no row for it, so no ancestor (the provisional *puni and Māori puni are dropped). Kept apart until P&E shows whether it is the same entry as "surrounded, overcome". Words punikoko, puniwaiwai.
puni#1.gloss_source: Wiktionary puni#1 "to be fond of, to be partial to; to desire, to covet"; Andrews 1922 puni n. 4 "a desire; a strong inclination"

puʻu.etymon_note: POLLEX PUKU.1A PPN *puku "protuberance, lump, joint, knot" (1C PCE "hill", same set); Wiktionary gives the same etymon. Andrews puts the throat here too, as in puʻukani. Not PUKU.3. Words puʻuwai, puʻuone, puʻukani, puʻukaua, puʻukoko, kuapuʻu.
puʻu.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) "protuberance, lump, swelling", "hill"; Wiktionary "hill, mound; pile; lump; joint"

pā#0.etymon_note: POLLEX PAA.1 PPN *paa "enclosure, fence, wall"; Wiktionary gives the same etymon. Māori is left out because POLLEX gives only the derived pāia. Words pākū, pānini.
pā#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) "enclosure, fence"; Wiktionary pā#0 "fence, wall, enclosure"

pā#4.etymon_note: POLLEX PAA.2B PPN *paa "strike against, hit; touch; reach" (P&E pāʻia) and PAA.2C PNP "blow against (of wind)" (P&E pā) are one set; Wiktionary pā#4 holds both. Words pāleo, pāleoleo (Wiktionary parts).
pā#4.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) pāʻia "touch, get, contact, reach, hit" and pā "blow (of wind)"; Wiktionary pā#4 "to touch, strike; to reach; to blow (as the wind)"

pā#plate.etymon_note: New stone for waʻapā, resolving pā?waʻapā: POLLEX PAA.4 PPN *paa "plate, platter, bowl" (P&E pā "dish, plate"), which Andrews joins to "board" in one sense. Not pā#0 fence or pā#4 touch. Tongan pā "shield" left out (POLLEX: uncertain).
pā#plate.gloss_source: Andrews 1922 waapa bracket "pa, a board"; Andrews pa n. 1 "a material having a flat surface, as a board, a plate, a server, a pan"; POLLEX (P&E) "dish, plate"

pāpale.etymon_note: No POLLEX set. Wiktionary: partial reduplication of pale "headdress", or pā + pale; Andrews brackets pa + pale "a defense". Its own stone, not linked to pale (B7 b, B10); no ancestor printed because the formation is uncertain. Word pāpale aliʻi.
pāpale.gloss_source: Wiktionary "hat, cap"; Andrews 1922 bracket "papale, hat" (pāpale aliʻi)

pāʻina.etymon_note: No POLLEX set; Wiktionary says -na is a nominaliser but no verb pāʻi exists, so no ancestor. Word papapāʻina.
pāʻina.gloss_source: Wiktionary "meal; dinner; small dinner party"; Andrews 1922 paina "a call to eat; a meal"

pī#sprinkle.etymon_note: New stone for pīkai, resolving pī?pīkai: Andrews names pi "to sprinkle". Not Wiktionary pī "stingy" (no etymology), which no shipped word uses. Spelled pī as in pīkai. No POLLEX set. Gloss is Andrews only (F1 placeholder until P&E).
pī#sprinkle.gloss_source: Andrews 1922 pikai bracket "pi, to sprinkle"; Andrews pi v. 1 "to sprinkle, as water; to throw water with the hand"

pō.etymon_note: POLLEX POO.1A PPN *poo "night" (1B "24-hour day", 1C PCE "the realm of the gods", same set); Wiktionary gives the same etymon. Card gloss stays "night, darkness". Words makapō, naʻaupō, pōʻele, ʻauinapō, kiaʻipō, luapō, Pōʻaono.
pō.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) "night"; Wiktionary "night, period of darkness"; Andrews 1922 "night; darkness"

pōhaku.etymon_note: POLLEX POO-FATU.1* PCE *poo-fatu "general term for stone or rock"; Wiktionary gives the same etymon. The Marquesan pohatu is left out because POLLEX flags it. Words kiʻi pōhaku, kālai pōhaku, papapōhaku, pōhakuhele, pōhaku paʻa.

pōʻai.etymon_note: POLLEX POOKAI PPN *pookai "to coil, wrap up"; Wiktionary gives the same etymon. Words pōʻailani (horizon), pōʻai lōʻihi, pōʻai puni, kahapōʻai.
pōʻai.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) "coil"; Wiktionary "to coil up; to encircle; circle, circuit"; Andrews 1922 "a circle; to encircle"

pū#0.etymon_note: pūkonakona uses "cluster, clump" (Wiktionary parts), POLLEX PUU.6 PCE *puu. Wiktionary pū#0 also holds "tree", which POLLEX files apart (PUQU PNP *puqu); no shipped word uses "tree", so no split now (a tree word would get pū#tree). Word pūkonakona.
pū#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) "cluster of several stalks; clump"; Wiktionary pū#0 "tree, cluster of several stalks; cluster, clump"

pū#1.etymon_note: POLLEX PUU.1 PPN *puu "trumpet shell; trumpet". Wiktionary derives pū "gun" (pū#2) from pū "conch" (pū#1) and Andrews has both in one entry, so pū#2 merges into pū#1. Tongan left out. Word panipū.
pū#1.gloss_source: Wiktionary pū "conch shell; any wind instrument" and "gun, pistol" (semantic extension); Andrews 1922 pu n. 1 "a conch; a trumpet", 2 "a gun, pistol"

pū?paʻapū.etymon_note: Left unresolved. The likeliest pū is the particle "together, completely" (POLLEX PUU.7 PCE *puu), which B1 rules out as a stone; if so the word drops. Not linked to pū#0 or pū#1.
pū?paʻapū.gloss_source: none: Wiktionary parses paʻapū as paʻa + pū "stand", a sense no pū entry has

pūpū#1.etymon_note: POLLEX PUUPUU.2 PPN *puupuu 'univalve shellfish' (cf. *puu 'shell trumpet'), a set apart from PUUPUU.4 'bundle' (pūpū#0, unused). Word panipūpū (eyestone shell).
pūpū#1.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Shell, snail"; Wiktionary "shell (marine or land), beads"

ua.etymon_note: POLLEX QUHA PPN *quha 'rain'; not the particles ua (perfect, *kua) or ua 'aforementioned' (*t-aua). Word waiua.

uhi#1.etymon_note: POLLEX QUFI.3 PPN *qufi 'cover up'; not QUFI.1 yam (uhi#0) and not PEP *uhi 'tattooing instrument', which Wiktionary files in the same entry. Words paleuhi, uhikino.
uhi#1.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Covering, cover, veil, lid"; Wiktionary "covering, veil; to cover"

uila.etymon_note: POLLEX QUHILA PPN *quhila 'lightning'. Word lolouila (computer, 'electric brain').

uli#0.etymon_note: POLLEX QULI.2 PPN *quli 'black, dark in colour', a set apart from QULI.1 'steer' (uli#1). Words aouli, kaiuli, nānāuli (Andrews' 'blue sky' is this sense). Andrews' uli n. 3 (a class of gods) is never printed.
uli#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Dark colour"; Wiktionary "any dark color (blue, green, black)"

uli#1.etymon_note: POLLEX QULI.1 PPN *quli 'to steer a vessel' (POc *quliŋ). Word hoe uli (steering paddle).
uli#1.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Steer v"; Wiktionary "to steer; steersman"

ulu#0.etymon_note: No ancestor printed: POLLEX files P&E's ulu 'to grow' under PPN *huru 'enter' (HURU.A) flagged Uncertain Semantic Connection, while Wiktionary derives it from *qulu, which POLLEX keeps for ulu 'grove' (QULU.2). Words laʻaulu, uluwehi.
ulu#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "To grow, increase, spread"; Wiktionary "growth; to grow"

waena.etymon_note: POLLEX WAHE-GA PPN *wahe-ŋa 'division, portion; middle'. Words anawaena, kikowaena, leowaena, papawaena.

waha#0.etymon_note: POLLEX PCE *waha 'mouth', a set apart from PCE *waha 'carry on the back' (waha#1, unused). Words haowaha, kaulawaha, paʻawaha, wahahewa, wahaheʻe, wahapaʻa.

wahine.etymon_note: POLLEX PCE *wahine 'woman, female'. Words aliʻiwahine, haku wahine, kupuna wahine, leo wahine.

wai#0.etymon_note: POLLEX WAI.1 PPN *wai 'fresh water'; not wai 'leave, deposit' (*qai, wai#1) or wai 'who' (*hai). 29 words, all the water sense: waimaka, waiū, kahawai, puʻuwai, ʻauwai and the rest.

wai#1.etymon_note: POLLEX QAI.1 PPN *qai "place, deposit, leave", the set that also holds P&E waiwai "goods, property, wealth, rich"; Wiktionary calls this derivation the more likely one. Not wai#0 "water" (WAI.1 *wai) or wai "who" (HAI *hai). Repeat waiwai is WAI·WAI on this stone and never links to the water words; the first-pass one-stone "waiwai" (puniwaiwai) stays separate (§4.4). The row Rapa Nui and Marquesan forms are problematic or unclear and are left out.
wai#1.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) wai "To retain, place, leave, remain, earn, deposit"; Wiktionary wai#1 "rare form of waiho (to leave, deposit)"

wailua.etymon_note: POLLEX WAI-RUA PEP *wai-rua 'spirit', an inherited compound kept as one stone (B6); never links to wai or lua. Word kino wailua.

waiwai.etymon_note: POLLEX files waiwai under QAI.1 PPN *qai 'place, deposit, leave' (via wai 'deposit'), not *wai 'water'; Wiktionary agrees ('more likely' wai 'leave'). A reduplicated stem as one stone (B7); never links to wai#0. Word puniwaiwai.
waiwai.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Goods, property... wealth... rich"; Wiktionary "to be rich"

waiū.etymon_note: POLLEX WAI-UU PNP *wai-uu 'milk', an inherited compound as one stone. Word waiūpaʻa; but waiū is also dealt as the two-stone word wai·ū, so B6 drops waiūpaʻa by default.

wale#only.etymon_note: New: POLLEX WALE.3 PPN *wale 'of no account, ordinary; only, just', the particle, a set apart from WALE.1, the secretion sense of the old wale id, which no word uses now and which must never print. Word kaʻawale. A particle stone exists only if B1 option 2 is chosen; the default ruling drops kaʻawale.
wale#only.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Postposed particle: only, just... alone; without payment, cause or reason"; Wiktionary particle "only, just, alone; for free"

wana.etymon_note: No POLLEX row for the single word. POLLEX WANA-WANA PPN *wana-wana "spiny, prickly" holds P&E wanawana "spiny, thorny" and notes "cf. PN *wana sea-urchin sp."; Wiktionary derives wana from PPN *wana. Cognates are the doubled forms in that row. Andrews wana v. "to appear, as light at dawn" (same as wena) is another word and not this stone. Word wanawana (spiny, like the urchin).
wana.gloss_source: Wiktionary wana "a sea urchin with long spines"; Andrews–Parker 1922 wana n. "a species of the sea-egg or sea-urchin", adj. "pronged; sharp pointed"

waʻa.etymon_note: POLLEX WAKA PPN *waka 'canoe'. Words auwaʻa, hoe waʻa, holowaʻa, waʻapā. Andrews' waa 'dig a furrow' (= waha) is not this stone.

wehe.etymon_note: POLLEX WESE PCE *wese "divide, separate" (P&E mawehe is the same set); Wiktionary has one homograph. Word wehewehe (to explain: to open up).
wehe.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Open, undo, untie, loosen"; Wiktionary wehe "to open; undo; take off; pull apart"

wehi.etymon_note: No ancestor printed: POLLEX's only Hawaiian wehi is P&E wehi 'dark' under PMQ *vehi (a moon phase, flagged uncertain), a different homograph from wehi 'adornment'. Word uluwehi.

welu.etymon_note: POLLEX WERU PCE *weru "ragged, frayed" holds both P&E welu and weluwelu "shredded to bits"; Andrews brackets weluwelu [Welu, a rag]. No Wiktionary entry, hence no earlier id; new id "welu" (bare root, untaken), as the reviewer proposed. Tahitian veruveru (POLLEX: uncertain semantic connection) and the Marquesan leaf-tip word are left out. Word weluwelu.
welu.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) welu "Rag, ragged garment; ragged, frayed"; Andrews–Parker 1922 welu "a rag of torn tapa or cloth"

wiki.etymon_note: POLLEX WITI PCE *witi "quick, lively"; Wiktionary gives *witi (attested only in Central-Eastern Polynesian). One homograph. Word wikiwiki.
wiki.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Hurry, hasten, quick, fast, swift"; Wiktionary wiki "to hasten; to be swift, quick"

wili.etymon_note: POLLEX WILI PPN *wili 'twist, turn; bore, drill'. Words lauwili, wiliʻau (form wiliau). Andrews' phrase for a disease under wili is never printed.
wili.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Wind, twist, writhe, crank, turn, screw, drill"; Wiktionary "to twist, wring; to bore"

wāwae.etymon_note: POLLEX WAQE PPN *waqe 'leg' lists Hawaiian wae and notes CE *wae(wae); wāwae is its reduplication (Wiktionary cognates Māori waewae, Tahitian ʻāvae), so no row matched the spelling. Words kaniwāwae, manamana wāwae.
wāwae.gloss_source: Wiktionary "leg, foot"; Andrews–Parker 1922 "the leg... the foot"

wī#famine.etymon_note: Split from Wiktionary wī#0, which lumps "famine" with "squeak; to squeal, tinkle" under one header with no etymology; the squeal sense is unrelated in meaning, unused, and must not share this stone. No POLLEX set for wī "famine"; POLLEX WII PPN *wii is the Spondias tree (wī#1) and is never the ancestor of this stone. Word wīwī (thin, lean), which Andrews derives from wi "famine"; P&E should confirm that derivation.
wī#famine.gloss_source: Wiktionary wī "famine"; Andrews–Parker 1922 wi n. "a famine; a destitution of food", adj. "impoverished", and wiwi v. bracket [Wi, famine]

ū#0.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *huhu 'breast, milk' (Wiktionary writes *susu); not ū 'drip, ooze' (ū#1). Word waiū.
ū#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Breast, teat, udder"; Wiktionary "breast; udder"

ʻaeʻa.etymon_note: No POLLEX set and no Wiktionary etymology; no ancestor given. Word hōkū ʻaeʻa (planet).

ʻaha#0.etymon_note: No POLLEX set for ʻaha 'assembly'; POLLEX's two ʻaha sets are *kafa 'sennit' (ʻaha#1) and *kafa 'mullet' (ʻaha#2), neither used, so no ancestor is printed. Words ʻahakanaka, ʻaha mele, ʻahaʻōlelo, ʻahāinu, ʻahāʻaina (forms ʻahainu, ʻahaʻaina; not ʻahā 'four').
ʻaha#0.gloss_source: Wiktionary "meeting, gathering, assembly"; Wiktionary etymologies of ʻahamele, ʻahaʻōlelo

ʻaha#1.etymon_note: POLLEX KAFA.1 PPN *kafa "sennit, coconut husk fibre". Not ʻaha#0 "assembly" (no POLLEX set), KAFA.2 *kafa "strong, great" or KAFA.3 *kafa "mullet" (ʻaha#2 needlefish). Wiktionary has three ʻahaʻaha: "cordage" (< ʻaha cord, this stone), "young of the needlefish" (< ʻaha#2) and a haughty sitting or standing posture (< *kafa "strong"). The posture word is the only ʻahaʻaha in POLLEX (P&E "stand in an overbearing manner", KAFA.2) and Andrews (ahaaha "sitting squarely"), so the "cordage" word rests on Wiktionary alone: P&E must confirm it. ʻahamaka (doubtful, "hammock") also names ʻaha#1.
ʻaha#1.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) ʻaha "Sennit"; Wiktionary ʻaha#1 "sennit; cord of braided sennit, hair"; Andrews–Parker 1922 aha n. 3 "a cord braided from the husk of the coconut"

ʻahu.etymon_note: POLLEX KAFU.A PPN *kafu 'covering, clothing'; not ahu 'heap' (*qafu, no ʻokina). Words ʻahuao (covering mat), ʻahu ʻula (feather cloak).
ʻahu.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Covering, clothing"; Wiktionary "cape, coat, any upper garment; covering; mat"

ʻahā.etymon_note: Wiktionary: ʻa- + hā 'four'. A derived numeral admitted as a stone (B12); POLLEX has no set for the derived form, so no ancestor is printed (the base hā is PPN *faa, FAA.1). Word ʻahālike.
ʻahā.gloss_source: Wiktionary "four; four times"; Andrews–Parker 1922 "the numeral four"

ʻai.etymon_note: POLLEX KAI PPN *kai 'food, eat'; the game-score set (also *kai) is not used. Words hoaʻai, holo ʻai, huaʻai, kuʻi ʻai, kēʻai, kōhiʻai, kūʻai, mahiʻai, paʻi ʻai, ʻaialo, ʻai kapu.
ʻai.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "To eat; food or food plant"; Wiktionary "food; to eat"

ʻaina#0.etymon_note: POLLEX KAI-GA.A PNP *kai-ŋa 'meal, feast'; not KAI-GA.B 'food refuse' or ʻāina 'land'. Words papa ʻaina, ʻahāʻaina.

ʻaka.etymon_note: POLLEX KATA PPN *kata 'laugh'; not Andrews' aka 'shadow' or 'but'. Word ʻakahenehene.

ʻaki#0.etymon_note: POLLEX KATI PPN *kati "bite, nip"; Wiktionary gives the same etymon. Not ʻaki#1 "pillow" (Andrews also lists "canoe stool", "knot of hair" and "height" under aki). Tahitian left out (modern spelling unsure). Word ʻakiʻaki (nibble, snap again and again).
ʻaki#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Bite, nip"; Wiktionary ʻaki#0 "to nip (take a bite and let go); to snap"

ʻale.etymon_note: POLLEX KALE.1 PNP *kale "a wave that ripples or breaks; ripple"; P&E ʻaleʻale is KALE-KALE.A PCE *kale-kale "agitated (of sea or water surface)", the doubled form of the same root. Wiktionary has one homograph. Andrews ale "to swallow" is not used. Sāmoan (problematic) and Marquesan (surface) left out. Word ʻaleʻale.
ʻale.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Wave, crest of a wave, billow; to ripple, form waves, stir"; Wiktionary ʻale "wave, billow; to ripple, to stir"

ʻalo.etymon_note: POLLEX KALO.1 PPN *kalo "dodge, evade"; Wiktionary gives the same etymon. Andrews alo "front; presence" (no ʻokina) is another spelling and stone (§4.4). Tahitian ʻaro (POLLEX: uncertain semantic connection) left out. Word ʻaloʻalo.
ʻalo.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Dodge, evade, elude, avoid"; Wiktionary ʻalo "to dodge, to evade"

ʻalu.etymon_note: POLLEX KALU PPN *kalu: KALU.A "loose or wrinkled membrane" (P&E ʻalu "loose skin over eyeball") and KALU.D PEP *kalu "loose, slack, wrinkled" (P&E ʻaluʻalu) are lettered sub-sets of one set, so one root (B8/B9); Wiktionary gives the same etymon. POLLEX KALU-KALU.B (a doubled set for "newborn") is not used here. Cognates: Māori karu, Tongan kalu (KALU.A), Rapa Nui karukaru "wrinkled" (KALU.D). Print only "slack, loose". Word ʻaluʻalu; hūʻalu (doubtful, "film over the eye") also names ʻalu.
ʻalu.gloss_source: Wiktionary ʻalu "to slacken, to relax; to hang, to sag"; POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) ʻaluʻalu "loose, flabby; slack, as a rope; wrinkled"

ʻaono.etymon_note: Wiktionary: ʻa- + ono 'six'. A derived numeral admitted as a stone (B12); POLLEX has no set for the derived form, so no ancestor is printed (the base ono is PPN *ono). Word Pōʻaono.

ʻape.etymon_note: POLLEX KAPE.1 PPN *kape (Alocasia macrorrhiza); Wiktionary has one homograph. Word ʻapeʻape (Gunnera, named for its likeness to ʻape; Andrews "a variety of the ape"). Wiktionary second ʻapeʻape (gill-like flapping) is unrelated and not this word.
ʻape.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) ʻape "(Alocasia macrorrhiza)"; Wiktionary ʻape "a large-leafed plant related to taro"; Wiktionary ʻapeʻape etymology "ʻape, giant taro"

ʻau#0.etymon_note: POLLEX KAU.4 PPN *kau 'stalk, stem, handle'; kūʻau is POLLEX *tuu-kau << *kau.4. ʻaulima is CE *kau-rima, which POLLEX compares with *kau.3 'wood' (no Hawaiian reflex); Andrews reads 'au, a handle'. The group sense Wiktionary lumps in here is now ʻau#group; ʻaumakua is withdrawn to ʻau?ʻaumakua.
ʻau#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Handle, staff, stem, stalk, shaft"; Wiktionary "handle; staff; stem; stalk"

ʻau#1.etymon_note: POLLEX KAU.1 PPN *kau 'swim'. Words kai ʻau (sea one must swim in), ʻaulike (swim abreast). ʻauwai is withdrawn to ʻau?ʻauwai; ʻauʻau 'bathe' is its own stone.
ʻau#1.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Swim"; Wiktionary "to swim, travel by sea"

ʻau#group.etymon_note: POLLEX KAU.2B PPN *kau "group of people, company", which P&E cites with ʻau waʻa itself. Word auwaʻa (form ʻauwaʻa). Same set as ʻaumoana (POLLEX >> CE *kau-moana); id to be shared with the ʻau batch.
ʻau#group.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Group (in ʻau waʻa, ʻau moku)"; Andrews–Parker 1922 bracket "au, a number"

ʻau?ʻaumakua.etymon_note: Unresolved, split from ʻau#0: POLLEX files ʻaumakua under PNP *kau-matua 'elderly man' with only 'Cf. *kau.2 group'; Wiktionary reads ʻau 'stem, stalk' (ʻau#0). Sources name different homographs (P18), so no link until P&E's Lit. Word ʻaumakua.
ʻau?ʻaumakua.gloss_source: none settled: Wiktionary ʻau 'stem, stalk'; POLLEX compares PPN *kau.2 'group, company'

ʻau?ʻauwai.etymon_note: Unresolved, withdrawn from ʻau#1 as the adjudication asks: Wiktionary reads ʻau 'swim', Andrews 'furrow' (back-formed, as for ʻauwaha); ʻauwai is not in POLLEX. Word ʻauwai.
ʻau?ʻauwai.gloss_source: none settled: Wiktionary ʻau 'to swim'; Andrews–Parker bracket 'au, furrow'

ʻauhau.etymon_note: POLLEX KAUFAU PCE *kaufau 'an ordered list or recitation' carries both P&E ʻauhau 'tax' and kūʻauhau 'genealogist', so one stone (B9): lunaʻauhau uses 'tax', kūʻauhau the older 'recitation' sense and needs its own parts-row gloss.
ʻauhau.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Price, tax, levy tax"; Wiktionary "tribute; tax"

ʻauina.etymon_note: Wiktionary: ʻaui 'to decline' + -na, a derived stem as one stone; no POLLEX set, so no ancestor. Words ʻauinalā, ʻauinapō.
ʻauina.gloss_source: Wiktionary "slope, decline, descent"; Andrews–Parker 1922 "descent; slope; declination"

ʻauʻau.etymon_note: POLLEX KAU-KAU PPN *kau-kau 'bathe', its own set; a reduplicated stem as one stone (B7), never linked to ʻau 'swim'. Word wai ʻauʻau.
ʻauʻau.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Bathe"; Wiktionary "to swim; to bathe"

ʻawa#bitter.etymon_note: New, split by sense: POLLEX KAWA.1B PNP *kawa "sour, bitter". Wiktionary and Andrews put this sense in one ʻawa entry with kava, which POLLEX files as the sister sub-set KAWA.1A (PPN *kawa, the plant and drink). The referents are disjoint (a taste, a plant), so the bitter sense gets its own id on the lima / lima#five precedent, and ʻawaʻawa never sits on the kava stone. The bare id ʻawa stays the kava stone (used by no word yet). Word ʻawaʻawa.
ʻawa#bitter.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) ʻawa "Sour, bitter"; Wiktionary ʻawa "sourness, bitterness"; Andrews–Parker 1922 awa n. 3 "the quality or state of being bitter"

ʻaʻa#0.etymon_note: POLLEX KAKA.1A PPN *kaka 'clothlike fibre at the base of coconut fronds' and KAKA.1B 'envelope' (bag, pocket) are sub-sets of one set, so one stone (B8, B9): ʻaʻaniu (frond sheath), ʻaʻapua (arrow bag). Not ʻaʻa 'brave' (*ma-kaka).
ʻaʻa#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Fibre from coconut husk"; "Bag, pocket, caul... chaff, hull"; Wiktionary "clothlike sheath at the base of a coconut frond; pocket, bag"

ʻeha.etymon_note: One Wiktionary entry with no etymology, and POLLEX has no Hawaiian row for ʻeha, so no ancestor is printed. Not ʻehā "four" (a different spelling and stone). Word ʻehaʻeha.
ʻeha.gloss_source: Wiktionary ʻeha "pain, ache, soreness", "hurt, sore, painful"; Andrews–Parker 1922 eha n. "injury … pain; sorrow", v. "to be hurt; to be sore"

ʻeke#cringe.etymon_note: New, split by etymon: POLLEX QETE PEP *qete "disgusted by", which also holds the P&E ʻekeʻeke "fussy, over-exacting, cranky". The bare Wiktionary id ʻeke merges this with ʻeke "bag" (POLLEX KETE.A PPN *kete, a separate set), so the bag sense keeps the bare id (used by no word yet). Rapa Nui and Marquesan reflexes omitted (sense drift); a Niuean form in the set is anatomical and is never printed. Word ʻekeʻeke.
ʻeke#cringe.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) ʻeke "Cringe, shrink from, draw away from, flinch, wince"; Wiktionary ʻeke v. "to cringe, draw away from, shrink from, wince"

ʻele.etymon_note: POLLEX KELE.C PEP *kele(-kele) 'dark, black', written ʻele(ʻele) in POLLEX, so no row matched. Its own stone, never linked to ʻeleʻele (§4.4). Words pōʻele, waiʻele.

ʻeleʻele.etymon_note: POLLEX KELE.C PEP *kele(-kele), reduplicated stem as one stone (B7), never linked to ʻele. Word wai ʻeleʻele (ink). Andrews' sense 2 under eleele is never printed (F1).

ʻie.etymon_note: New, provisional. The base is attested only by the Andrews headword ie n. 2 (the same Freycinetia vine); the ʻokina is taken from the doubled form, which P&E (via POLLEX) and Wiktionary spell ʻieʻie. POLLEX files ʻieʻie under KIE-KIE.B PNP *kie-kie and notes that set comes from PN *kie "Pandanus sp."; Wiktionary says the same. POLLEX has no Hawaiian row for the bare root, so the cognates are the KIE-KIE.B reflexes of the doubled plant name. P&E should confirm ʻie as a free word and its spelling. Other Andrews ie senses (canvas, braid, insult) are not this stone. Word ʻieʻie.
ʻie.gloss_source: Andrews–Parker 1922 ie n. 2 "A tall woody climber (Freycinetia arnotti), a tough, wiry vine used in tying and in basketwork. See ieie"; POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) ʻieʻie "Plant sp. (Freycinetia arborea)"

ʻike.etymon_note: POLLEX KITE.A PPN *kite 'see, know', written ʻike-a in POLLEX, so no row matched. Word ʻikepili (data). Andrews' sense 4 (a biblical euphemism) is never printed (A1).
ʻike.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) ʻike-a "See, know, feel"; Wiktionary "sight; knowledge; to see, to know"

ʻili.etymon_note: POLLEX KILI.1 PPN *kili "skin; bark"; "surface" is the same word (P&E ʻilikai < PCE *kiri-a-tai "surface of the sea"). Not Andrews' ili "run aground" (POLLEX HILI, no ʻokina), and the land-division sense is not used. Words hueʻili, ʻililua (skin), ʻilikai, paʻaʻili (surface).
ʻili.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Skin"; Wiktionary "skin; peel, bark, rind; surface"; POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) ʻilikai "surface of the sea"

ʻimo.etymon_note: New: POLLEX KIMO PCE *kimo "wink" holds both P&E ʻimo "to wink" and ʻimoʻimo "to twinkle" (and ʻiʻimo "to blink"). The base is P&E via POLLEX, so the stone needs no further source. Word ʻimoʻimo.
ʻimo.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) ʻimo "To wink"; Andrews–Parker 1922 imo v. 1 "To wink", v. 3 "To twinkle, as a star"

ʻino.etymon_note: POLLEX KINO PPN *kino "bad"; one Wiktionary entry. Tongan kinohaʻa (POLLEX) left out on purpose. Words lokoʻino, manawaʻino, moeʻino.
ʻino.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Wicked, spoiled, ugly"; Wiktionary "bad, wicked"

ʻiwa#fern.etymon_note: New, split by sense: POLLEX KIWA.2A PCE *kiwa "a fern (Asplenium)", which also holds the P&E ʻiwaʻiwa "maidenhair ferns". The frigatebird is the sister sub-set KIWA.2B; Wiktionary merges both in one ʻiwa entry and leads with the bird. The referents are disjoint, so the fern gets its own id (lima / lima#five precedent) and the bare id ʻiwa stays the frigatebird (used by no word yet). Word ʻiwaʻiwa.
ʻiwa#fern.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) ʻiwa "A fern (Asplenium horridum)"; Wiktionary ʻiwa "any member of the species Asplenium horridum of ferns"

ʻiʻiwi.etymon_note: A bird name with no POLLEX set and no Wiktionary etymology, so no ancestor is printed. Word huluʻiʻiwi.
ʻiʻiwi.gloss_source: Wiktionary "iiwi, scarlet honeycreeper"; Andrews–Parker 1922 bracket "iiwi, a small red bird" (huluiiwi)

ʻiʻo#0.etymon_note: POLLEX KIKO.A PPN *kiko "flesh" quotes P&E's single ʻiʻo entry, which runs from "flesh, meat" through "essence, substance" to "true, genuine". So Wiktionary's ʻiʻo#1 "true" ("perhaps from the preceding") is the same etymon as ʻiʻo#0 "flesh" and is merged into it (B8, B9: one root, per-word gloss). Word manaʻoʻiʻo.
ʻiʻo#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) ʻiʻo "... essence, substance; heart or gist of a matter; true, genuine"; Wiktionary ʻiʻo "true, genuine"; Andrews–Parker 1922 bracket "io, real; substantial"

ʻohana#0.etymon_note: POLLEX KOO-FAGA PCE *koo-faŋa "nest"; Wiktionary agrees (PPN *kofa-ŋa "nest"). One derived stem as one stone (B6); not ʻohā, a different spelling. Māori is written kōhanga as Wiktionary gives it (POLLEX koowhanga). ʻohana#1 "family prayers" is not used. Word lunaʻohana.
ʻohana#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Family, kin group; related"; Wiktionary "family, relatives, kin group"

ʻohe.etymon_note: POLLEX KOFE.A PPN *kofe "bamboo sp." holds both P&E ʻohe "bamboo" and P&E ʻoheʻohe "tall native tree" in the same sub-set, so the tree sense is the same root (B9) and keeps the id ʻohe. The gloss is the tree sense ʻoheʻohe keeps; the P&E row for the base gives only "bamboo", so the P&E check should confirm the tree sense of ʻohe. A bamboo compound added later shares this id and needs its own per-word gloss (B9). Cognates are bamboo words. Word ʻoheʻohe.
ʻohe.gloss_source: Andrews–Parker 1922 ohe n. 3 "A tree 40-80 feet high (Tetraplasandra Hawaiiensis)", n. 6 "A tree (Reynoldsia sandwicensis)"; Wiktionary ʻoheʻohe "Reduplication of ʻohe (Polyscias sandwicensis)"; POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) ʻoheʻohe "Tall native tree sp. (Tetraplasandra spp.)"

ʻohā.etymon_note: Wiktionary derives it from PPN *kofa, but POLLEX has no Hawaiian ʻohā row, so no ancestor is printed. Andrews' oha "lovesick" and "salutation" are another word (POLLEX OFA oha "affection, greeting", no ʻokina or kahakō) and never reach this stone. Word ʻohākulaʻi.
ʻohā.gloss_source: Wiktionary "taro corm growing from the older root; offspring"; Andrews–Parker 1922 "small sprigs of taro that grow on the sides of the older roots"

ʻoi.etymon_note: POLLEX KOI.2 PCE *koi "sharp". Andrews has "superiority, be better" and "sharp edge, be sharp" in one entry, and Wiktionary links ʻoihana's ʻoi "main" to the *koi entry, so it is one word. P&E should confirm that "best" is not a separate homograph. Not KOI.3 PPN *koi "while" (a particle). Word ʻoihana.
ʻoi.gloss_source: Wiktionary ʻoihana "ʻoi (main) + hana (work)"; Andrews–Parker 1922 oi n. "excess; superiority", v. "to be more; to be better" (one entry with "sharp")

ʻoli.etymon_note: POLLEX KOLI.1B PPN *koli "to dance; rejoice, be happy". P&E (via POLLEX) splits hauʻoli as hau/ʻoli, so it is ʻoli "joy", not Andrews' oli "chant". The Māori form POLLEX lists is left out on purpose (irregular, and its sense must not be printed). Same POLLEX set as ʻoni (KOLI.1A), but a different spelling, so a different stone (B10). Word hauʻoli.
ʻoli.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Joy, happiness, pleasure; happy, joyful"; Wiktionary "joy, happiness, pleasure"

ʻolu.etymon_note: New, provisional: attested by the Andrews headword olu and by the Wiktionary etymology of ʻoluʻolu; the spelling ʻolu is the P&E form in POLLEX. POLLEX cites P&E ʻolu only as "supple, flexible" under KOLU PNP *kolu "curved, coiled". Andrews has both senses under one word, but no source says "pleasant" is the *kolu root, so no ancestor or cognates are printed until P&E settles it. An Andrews-only noun sense ("sensual pleasure") is a P&E gate under A1 and is never printed. Word ʻoluʻolu.
ʻolu.gloss_source: Wiktionary ʻoluʻolu "Reduplication of ʻolu (to be pleasant, comfortable)"; Andrews–Parker 1922 olu adj. 1 "Cool; refreshing. Comfortable; easy; pleasant", v. 1 "To feel well disposed; to be agreeable"

ʻona.etymon_note: POLLEX KONA.3 PPN *kona "intoxicating, poisonous; intoxicated"; Wiktionary agrees (one entry). P&E ʻona "satiated, satisfied" is a separate set (KONA.2 PNP *kona) and not this stone. Word ʻonaʻona (dizzy, faint).
ʻona.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) ʻona "Drunk, dizzy and unsteady; intoxicating, intoxication"; Wiktionary ʻona "drunk; intoxicating"

ʻoni.etymon_note: New: POLLEX KOLI.1A PNP *koli "to move" (variant *ko(l,n)i; Wiktionary writes *koni), the same protoform the curated ʻoniʻoni stone prints. KOLI.1B ("dance, rejoice", Hawaiian ʻoli) is a different word; its Māori reflex is never printed. Tahitian ori omitted (modern spelling uncertain). ʻONI and the stone ʻONIʻONI (kiʻiʻoniʻoni) never link: different spellings (§4.4, B10). Word ʻoniʻoni.
ʻoni.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) ʻoni "To move, fidget, wriggle"; Andrews–Parker 1922 oni v. 1 "To move; to stir"

ʻoniʻoni.etymon_note: Reduplication of ʻoni (Wiktionary), which POLLEX files under KOLI.1A PNP *koli "to move" (variant *ko(l,n)i; Wiktionary writes *koni). Like other reduplicated stems it is a stone of its own (B7) and never links to ʻoli. 8 characters, at B11's cap. Word kiʻiʻoniʻoni.
ʻoniʻoni.gloss_source: Wiktionary "to move back and forth; to move constantly; movement"; POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) ʻoni "to move, fidget, wriggle"

ʻopi.etymon_note: POLLEX KOPI.A PPN *kopi "double together, fold"; Wiktionary agrees (one etymology). Māori kopi itself is left out because of one of its glosses; kokopi "double together, shut" stands in. Word ʻopiʻopi.
ʻopi.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) ʻopi "Fold, crease; wrinkled; bend of a wave"; Wiktionary ʻopi "to fold, to crease"; Andrews–Parker 1922 opi v. "To fold up, as tapa or cloth"

ʻuala.etymon_note: POLLEX KUMALA.1 PN *ku(u)mala "sweet potato" (from the local POLLEX page cache; the batch input had no row). POLLEX marks the Hawaiian form Problematic because the m is lost, but the etymon is not in doubt; Wiktionary agrees (PPN *kumala). Word ʻualakahiki.
ʻuala.gloss_source: Wiktionary "sweet potato"; POLLEX KUMALA.1 (Pukui & Elbert) ʔU(w)ala "Sweet potato (Ipomoea batatas)"

ʻuhane.etymon_note: POLLEX KUHANE PEP *kuhane "ghost, soul, spirit"; an East Polynesian word, so there are no Māori, Tahitian or Sāmoan cognates in the set. Word moeʻuhane.
ʻuhane.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Soul, spirit, ghost"; Wiktionary "soul, spirit"

ʻuki.etymon_note: New, provisional. The base is attested only by the Andrews headword uki n. 1 (Dianella), whose entry also names several other plants; the ʻokina comes from the Wiktionary spelling of ʻukiʻuki. No POLLEX row and no etymology anywhere, so no ancestor. No source says ʻukiʻuki is uki doubled. Andrews prints no plant sense under ukiuki, only "vexed; contempt; an offensive odor", so P&E must confirm the plant word and say which sense leads (F1). Other Andrews uki senses (a smell, to wring) are not this stone and are never printed. Word ʻukiʻuki.
ʻuki.gloss_source: Andrews–Parker 1922 uki n. 1 "A small shrub (Dianella odorata). Flowers somewhat sweet scented"; Wiktionary ʻukiʻuki "Dianella sandwicensis of flax lilies"

ʻuku#0.etymon_note: POLLEX KUTU.1 PPN *kutu "louse". Not Andrews' uku "pay, wages" (POLLEX UTU.1A, no ʻokina); ʻuku#1 "small" is not used. Words ʻukulele, ʻukupoʻo.

ʻula#0.etymon_note: POLLEX KULA.1A PPN *kula "red". KULA.1C "sacred, regal" (Wiktionary ʻula#1) and Wiktionary's ʻula#2 "blood" are the same set, so one root (B8). ʻahuʻula links here whether P&E reads it "red" (Andrews) or "sacred" (Wiktionary); its per-word gloss waits for P&E (B9). Words hamoʻula, kōʻula, maʻaweʻula, ʻahuʻula.

ʻula?alaʻula.etymon_note: Unresolved. The word is spelled alaula with no ʻokina (the review counts that spelling as corroborated, and words.js ships it), so the stone is ULA, not ʻula "red" (B10). The ʻ in the id is the old guess and is kept only because ids are never changed silently. P&E's ula "flame" (POLLEX ULA.1A PPN *ula) would fit "dawn light, sunset glow", but no source says which ula alaula uses, so no gloss or ancestor is printed. Word alaʻula.
ʻula?alaʻula.gloss_source: none settled: Andrews–Parker 1922 bracket "ula, red" (Andrews marks no ʻokina); POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) ula "flame, to flame"

ʻulu.etymon_note: POLLEX KULU.1 PPN *kulu "breadfruit". Not ulu "grow" (no ʻokina, batch-07's ulu#0). Words lauʻulu, ʻulukahiki.

ʻā#0.etymon_note: POLLEX KAHA.1 PPN *kaha "to burn". ʻā#1 (drive animals, booby, damselfish, the letter) is unrelated and not used. Word oneʻā (spelling inferred from Andrews' bracket).
ʻā#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Fiery, burning; fire: to burn, blaze"; Wiktionary "fire, burning; to burn"

ʻāina.etymon_note: POLLEX KAAIGA PPN *kaaiŋa "place of residence, home". Andrews' aina "meal; refuse" is modern ʻaina, another spelling and stone. Words anaʻāina, hakuʻāina, hoaʻāina, kahuʻāina, kiaʻāina, komoʻāina, kuaʻāina, kālaiʻāina, mokuʻāina.
ʻāina.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Land, earth"; Wiktionary "land (earth; country; real estate)"

ʻākau.etymon_note: POLLEX KATAU PCE *katau "right (not left)". Word limaʻākau.
ʻākau.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Right (not left)"; Wiktionary "right (not left); north"

ʻē#1.etymon_note: POLLEX KEHE PPN *kehe "different, other". P&E's kūʻē is a POLLEX compound in its own right (PPN *tuqu-kehe "be different"). Not POLLEX EE "yes" or Wiktionary's ʻē#0 (the letter). Word kūʻē.

ʻēʻē#0.etymon_note: Reduplication of ʻē "different" < PPN *kehe (Wiktionary; Andrews sets ee beside e in kuee). The only POLLEX ʻēʻē row, KEEKEE PCE *keekee, is the other homograph (ʻēʻē#1) and is not attached. A reduplicated stem as one stone (B7), not linked to ʻē#1. Word kūʻēʻē.
ʻēʻē#0.gloss_source: Wiktionary "peculiar; contrary, opposite"; Andrews–Parker 1922 ee adv. "in a contrary manner; adversely"

ʻō#0.etymon_note: POLLEX KOHO PPN *koho "digging stick, husking stake", the set that also holds P&E ʻōʻō "digging-stick"; Wiktionary ʻō#0 gives the same etymon and calls ʻō and ʻōʻō doublets. Not ʻō "to hail" (KOO.2B), ʻō "to fly, as a kite" (KOO.3), the ʻō- prefix (KOO-.3) or ʻō#1 (the letter name). Same set as the curated stone ʻōʻō#1 but a different spelling, so they never link (§4.4, B10). Words ʻōʻō (repeat); also ʻōhewa and ʻōkoholā (not live).
ʻō#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) ʻō "Sharp-pointed stick, coconut husker"; Wiktionary ʻō "special planted stick for husking coconuts; pin, spear, any piercing instrument", "to pierce"

ʻōlelo.etymon_note: POLLEX KOO-LELO PNP *koo-lelo "speak, orate, recite", which settles Wiktionary's two options in favour of the *kolelo one (Māori kōrero). Words hakuʻōlelo, hoaʻōlelo, huaʻōlelo, kakaʻōlelo, lunaʻōlelo, moʻoʻōlelo, poʻoʻōlelo, ʻahaʻōlelo, ʻōleloaʻo, ʻōlelopaʻa.
ʻōlelo.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Language, speech, word"; Wiktionary "language, speech; word, term"

ʻōpū.etymon_note: POLLEX KOOPUU.B PEC *koopuu "gullet, stomach, belly, guts"; Wiktionary writes PPN *kuupoo. The gloss leads with "belly". The other anatomical senses in the entry are never printed. Words ʻōpūao, ʻōpūhao, ʻōpūhue.
ʻōpū.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Belly, stomach, abdomen"; Wiktionary "stomach, belly"

ʻōʻō#1.etymon_note: POLLEX KOHO PPN *koho "digging stick, husking stake". Not ʻōʻō#0, the bird (onomatopoeic; POLLEX KOOKOO.1 PEC *kookoo). ʻō "pierce" is the same set but a different spelling and stone. Words ʻōʻōahi, ʻōʻōhao, ʻōʻōhou.

alahaka.reason: POLLEX (P&E) alahaka "plank bridge, ladder" < PCE *ara-fata "bridge or ladder", cf. PPN *fata "shelf": haka "shelf, platform" (haka#0), not haka "gap".

alapiʻi.reason: Unchanged: ala "path" + piʻi "climb" (PEP *piki); restored by the A4 default (P&E via POLLEX has only "climb, ascend").

anilā.reason: lā#2 (day) merged into lā#1: POLLEX sun (LAQAA.A) and day (LAQAA.B) are one set, PPN *laqaa; Wiktionary derives both from *laqa.

aumoe.reason: POLLEX (P&E) and Wiktionary derive aumoe from *aqu-mohe "fast asleep", not *qau "current"; Andrews reads au "time". Split off the current stone, left unresolved.

auwaʻa.reason: Form ʻauwaʻa; POLLEX (P&E) glosses ʻau "group (in ʻau waʻa)" < PPN *kau "group of people". Not au "current".

haomanamana.reason: manamana#1 (branching) merged into manamana#0: both are reduplicated *maŋa "branch" (Wiktionary; POLLEX MAGA-MAGA.B, from *maŋa); Andrews reads the finger as the branch of the hand.

hauʻoli.reason: POLLEX (P&E) lists hau/ʻoli under PPN *sau "(in compounds) temperament"; Wiktionary agrees. Not hau "dew" or "hibiscus".

holoʻai.reason: Resolved: Andrews brackets holo 'bundle' and POLLEX (P&E) has holo 'a long bundle, as of hard poi' (PNP *solo, SOLO.2B), a set apart from holo 'run'.

huamele.reason: Resolved: Andrews brackets hua 'letter' and POLLEX (P&E) has hua 'word, letter, figure' apart from *fua 'fruit'; the two agree, so hua?huamele becomes hua#word (A2).

huaʻōlelo.reason: Split of the old hua id: the word means 'word' and P&E's hua 'word, letter' (POLLEX, apart from *fua) is the root A2 assigns it. Wiktionary reads hua 'seed, fruit' and the adjudicator had left it unresolved; the P&E check should confirm.

kahawai.reason: Withdrawn from kaha#1: Wiktionary reads kaha 'place', Andrews 'cut'; the adjudication and P18 say a sense id only when sources agree, so the link to kahakai and kahaone waits for P&E's Lit.

kahuahi.reason: Resolved: POLLEX puts kahu 'keeper' and kahu 'tend an oven' in one set (PPN *tafu, TAFU.A–C, and PMQ *tafu(-afi), Marquesan tahuahi 'servant who lights the fire'), so either reading is the same root as kahu akua and kahu ʻāina.

kaipiʻi.reason: Unchanged: POLLEX (P&E) kai piʻi "high or rising tide" < PCE *tai-pii; P&E ʻokina fits piʻi "rise" (< *piki), so piʻi#0 stands.

kalahale.reason: Resolved: POLLEX (P&E) kala hale 'house gable' < PPN *tara 'end wall of a house', and Andrews' kala n. 3 'the ends of a house'; a fifth kala, apart from the *tala sets.

kaʻawale.reason: Resolves wale?kaʻawale: Wiktionary's kaʻa + wale 'alone' and P&E via POLLEX (WALE.3) name the particle 'only, alone', not the secretion noun (WALE.1). B1 still decides whether the word ships (default: drop).

keikipapa.reason: Andrews bracket "papa, an ancestor" is the genealogy/stratum sense of PAPA.1C (same set as board); Wiktionary splits papa senses by entry, not etymon (it splits class and list too). P&E to confirm.

kikolā.reason: lā#2 (day) merged into lā#1: POLLEX LAQAA.A sun / LAQAA.B day are one set.

koikahi.reason: Resolved: Andrews' koi n. 'ax; adze' sends the reader to its compounds; the tool word takes koʻi 'adze' (P&E spelling, PPN *toki), as the form koʻikahi already does.

koilipi.reason: Resolved: koʻi 'adze, axe' (PPN *toki) + lipi 'sharp edge' for an axe; Andrews' koi n. 'ax; adze' points to this compound. Form koʻilipi.

kūkulupapa.reason: kūkulu#1 merged into kūkulu#0: POLLEX (P&E) glosses one kūkulu 'pillar, post; to build a house' (PNP *tulu-tulu).

laelua.reason: lae#1 merged into lae#0: POLLEX forehead (LAQE.A) and promontory (LAQE.B) are one set, PPN *laqe.

laupapa.reason: Resolves lau?laupapa: POLLEX (P&E) files laupapa under PPN *lau 'expanse, breadth' and as PPN *lau-papa 'broad flat surface', not lau 'leaf'.

lawakua.reason: Resolves lawa?lawakua: Andrews' bracket 'lawa, to bind' is POLLEX/P&E lawa 'bind' (PPN *lawa, LAWA.2), not lawa 'enough'.

laʻamake.reason: Resolves laʻa?laʻamake: Andrews defines it 'time when vegetables die', his laʻa n. 'season'; shares the stone with laʻaulu (provisional until P&E).

laʻaulu.reason: Resolves laʻa?laʻaulu: Andrews defines it 'time when vegetables grow fast', his laʻa n. 'season'; shares the stone with laʻamake (provisional until P&E).

lunakoa.reason: Split of koa#0: 'soldier' (Andrews' bracket) belongs with brave/warrior under PPN *toqa (POLLEX), not with the koa tree (*toa).

lāhana.reason: lā#2 (day) merged into lā#1: POLLEX LAQAA.A sun / LAQAA.B day are one set.

manaʻoʻiʻo.reason: Merge ʻiʻo#1 into ʻiʻo#0: POLLEX KIKO.A quotes P&E's one ʻiʻo entry, which gives "true, genuine" together with "flesh", so it is one etymon, PPN *kiko. The stone keeps the gloss "true, genuine" for this word. manaʻo is unchanged.

moʻoaliʻi.reason: Andrews bracket [Moo, a line, and alii, chief]: moʻo "line, succession", not the lizard.

moʻokanaka.reason: Andrews: a genealogy or list of the people; moʻo "line" (bracket OCR live = line).

moʻokupuna.reason: Andrews bracket [Moo, line, and kupuna]: line of ancestors.

moʻokūʻauhau.reason: Andrews bracket [Moo, a line, and kuauhau]: line of descent.

moʻoʻōlelo.reason: Andrews bracket [Moo, line, and olelo, discourse]; moʻolelo is its contraction (succession of talk).

palaimaka.reason: Andrews bracket [Palai, to turn away, and maka, face] and Andrews verb palai "turn the face away"; not fern or fry.

panepoʻo.reason: POLLEX PANE.A (P&E pane "hind part of the head") and Andrews pane "joining of head and neck" settle it: not pane "answer".

panipū.reason: pū "gun" is a semantic extension of pū "conch" (Wiktionary, Andrews): pū#2 renamed to pū#1, PPN *puu.

papamanamana.reason: manamana#1 (branching) merged into manamana#0: one etymon, reduplicated *maŋa "branch".

pipiwai.reason: Andrews bracket "pipi, to percolate, and wai, water"; neither pipi oyster nor pipi beef. Stone spelled pīpī.

pīkai.reason: Andrews bracket "pi, to sprinkle, and kai, salt water"; not pī "stingy".

waipiʻi.reason: Unchanged: wai "water" + piʻi "rise" (flood, overflowing water); restored by the A4 default.

waʻapā.reason: Andrews bracket "pa, a board"; pā "flat object: board, plate" (POLLEX PAA.4), not fence or touch.

wiliʻau.reason: Resolves ʻau?wiliʻau: form wiliau has no ʻokina, so not ʻau 'swim'; Andrews' au n. 'current... circular motion, as caused by an eddy' is the word's own meaning. B10 names au 'current' (wiliau); batch-00's au (PPN *qau).

ʻaumakua.reason: Split from ʻau#0: Wiktionary reads ʻau 'stem, stalk', POLLEX's *kau-matua only compares *kau.2 'group'. Different homographs named (P18), so no link to ʻaulima or ʻaumoana until P&E's Lit.

ʻaumoana.reason: Resolves ʻau?ʻaumoana: POLLEX lists P&E ʻau-moana 'sailor' as CE *kau-moana << PN *kau.2 'group, company' (and KAU.2B >> *kau-moana); Andrews' 'au, to swim' is a 1922 bracket (F2). Shares batch-00's ʻau#group with auwaʻa.

ʻauwai.reason: Withdrawn from ʻau#1 as the adjudication asks: Wiktionary 'swim' vs Andrews 'furrow', not in POLLEX; 'a sense too weak to support a Lit. is too weak to support a stone link'. wai#0 unchanged.
